h: Daas Unites the Mind and Heart in Torah

p: "There is gold and an abundance of pearls,
but the lips of knowledge are a precious vessel," etc.;
"If you have acquired knowledge, what do you lack?" etc.;
everyone brought their donation to the Mishkan,
this is the donation of the Nesi'im, etc.;
and he said, "Everyone brought their donation,
HaKadosh Baruch Hu said to him:
"By your life, your speech is dearer to Me
to Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
in not having brought a donation of gold?
anything to bring at the time,
that all Yisrael were busy with the spoils of Mitzrayim,
while he was busy with the bones of Yosef;
and did not Chazal, of blessed memory, say
that "soul" is said of the poor man's meal-offering,
as though he offered his very soul?
the crown of kingship and the crown of priesthood;
which is alluded to by the Shulchan in the north,
דְּזֵר שֶׁל שֻׁלְחָן הוּא כֶּתֶר מַלְכוּת
that the crown of the Shulchan is the crown of kingship;
This is the aspect of fear and self-restraint,
to which Chazal, of blessed memory, alluded
"One who wishes to become wealthy should face north";
meaning, one who is in the aspect of north,
and through this he merited wealth.
And this is the trait of kingship:
a surpassing degree of fear and submission in the heart,
actual wealth of gold as well,
who does not come to poverty."
And this is the fear that is in the heart,
but has no fear of Heaven;
and as is stated in Sefer Yetzirah (chapter 6):
is like a king in his country.
corresponds to the crown of priesthood,
And so it was in actual fact,
for the garments of the Kohen Gadol.
And this is the aspect of Chochmah in the mind,
which is the neshamah in the mind,
in which there is never any blemish or corruption,
"The soul You have placed within me is pure."
And this is the aspect of Aharon HaKohen,
no sin or iniquity at all;
כִּי גַּם הַחֵטְא שֶׁל מֵי מְרִיבָה
for even the sin of Mei Merivah,
"Because you did not believe in Me,"
it is stated about this in the Midrash
who came to take the threshing floor of the borrower,
and took his and his neighbor's;
"if he sins to the guilt of the people";
for even the inadvertent sin that befell him
is not like that of other people,
"and God caused it to come to his hand,"
through a cause of his own;
rather, the cause for the Kohen
stems from the guilt of the community.
And therefore it does not say regarding his offering,
"and he shall be forgiven for his sin which he sinned,"
as is said of all the others.
The holy Ramban took note of this
and wrote that it is because,
the atonement is not completed by this.
But one can say, in line with our words,
that it is because he has no need for atonement,
since the sin did not come from his side.
"but the lips of knowledge are a precious vessel";
for Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
that is, to kingship and priesthood,
And about this it was said to him:
"but the lips of knowledge are a precious vessel";
"If you have acquired knowledge, what do you lack?"
For the aspect of kingship by itself,
which is the Binah in the heart,
through the heart of the fool,
who were not as they should have been;
and also to the aspect of priesthood,
which is the Chochmah in the mind alone,
from which come the sources of life to the mind;
which joins the Chochmah in the mind
with the will in the heart;
and through this it is guarded
"And the lips of a kohen guard knowledge."
And this is the main power
of Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him:
which is the crown of Torah;
as is stated in the Midrash
which pertain specifically to the Kohanim;
and Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him, thought
that he had no connection at all
That is why it says here specifically
that the essence of the holiness of Toras Kohanim
which is the aspect of Da'as
that binds the mind to the heart,
in line with our words above.
